name: R2AI2026 ViBioMIR Scoring Program and Metric Engineering
approach: FINAL_SCORE = mean(DOCS_F2MACRO, CHUNKS_F2MACRO); F2 = 5PR/(4P+R), per-query, macro-averaged (equal weight per query). (a) rapidfuzz.distance.LCSseq.similarity(c,g) returns the length of the longest common subsequence (order-preserving, NOT requiring contiguity). Live-verified: LCSseq.similarity("abxcd","abycdf") = 4. The rapidfuzz.distance.LCSseq module has existed since v2.0.0 (2022) and is stable through 2.15.x and 3.x. The scorer does NOT use fuzz.ratio/partial_ratio/token_sort_ratio (those are edit-distance/token-ratio based). It also does NOT use LCSseq.normalized_similarity, because that divides by max(len1,len2); instead the scorer computes overlap = LCSseq.similarity(c,g) / len(g), i.e. it divides by the GOLD chunk token length |g| (asymmetric, recall-style). (b) tokenizers 0.13.3 (HF tokenizers lib, ~May-2023) tokenizes chunk text before LCS. The library supports WordPiece (BERT), Unigram/SentencePiece (XLM-R, BGE-M3), BPE (GPT, underthesea), and simple whitespace/word or char tokenizers. Vietnamese is not word-segmented well by BERT-style subword tokenizers; XLM-R/BGE-M3 split Vietnamese into subword pieces. Because |g| = number of gold-chunk tokens, the 0.40 threshold means at least 40% of the gold chunk tokens must appear in order (as a subsequence) within the submitted chunk. WHICH tokenizer the scorer loads is the single biggest scoring-clarity risk (see uncertain scorer_tokenizer_identity). (c) Edge cases: query with |G|=0 -> doc-level R = 0/0 division-by-zero; the likeliest handling is F2=0 or skip-query (UNCERTAIN; if it skips, no-gold queries can be ignored; if it assigns F2=0, must avoid submitting to them). Empty D (no submitted docs) -> P=0/0, likeliest F2=0/skipped. A chunk for a doc_id NOT in G can never match any gold chunk (matching restricted to same query + same doc_id) so it always counts incorrect for chunk precision. A submitted chunk overlapping >=0.40 with MULTIPLE gold chunks (same doc) counts as correct ONCE (precision is binary per submitted chunk; no double-counting of numerator). A gold chunk found by MULTIPLE submitted chunks counts once for recall (recall counts each gold chunk at most once; "found" = exists >=1 matching submitted chunk). Macro-average: equal weight to every query regardless of gold count; queries with more gold chunks dominate chunk-recall contribution by chunk counts but not by query weight. (d) Legal strategic consequences: F2 beta=2 favors RECALL (recall weighted 2.5x over precision). Because LCSseq is NOT contiguous, a large submitted chunk (e.g. whole document) will contain any gold chunk tokens in order, so overlap(c,g) ~ 1.0 -> it "finds" the gold chunk. Thus one whole-doc chunk per predicted-gold doc collapses the chunk metric to a doc decision: chunk-recall ~ share of gold chunks living in submitted docs, chunk-precision ~ share of submitted docs actually containing gold. Large chunks are recall-optimal; small/overlapping windows multiply the precision denominator for no recall gain. Dedup: submitting the same/duplicate chunk twice is pure waste (adds a denominator count, no new correct count) -> never submit duplicates. Within a doc, submit exactly ONE whole-doc chunk (or few high-precision chunks); extra chunks only hurt precision. Top-k without labels: F2 is a recall-vs-precision tradeoff; because recall is weighted 2.5x, bias k UP vs a precision-optimal k. For expected small gold-per-query (likely 3-10 in a medical retrieval eval), overshooting hurts precision roughly linearly while the last extra gold doc helps recall only by its share; the sweet spot is slightly above the expected gold count, refined via pseudo-labeling. Net: the chunk metric acts essentially as a doc-level metric when you emit one whole-doc chunk per doc, so tune at the DOC level then emit one whole-doc chunk each.
languages: vi/en/zh (Latin-script). Normalization NFKC + HTML-entity decode + lowercase + whitespace collapse + trim applies to all languages before tokenizing.
benchmark_scores: Baseline (BM25) on this competition: docs F2 0.5587, chunks F2 0.1941, FINAL_SCORE ~0.3764. The metric itself is not a model with separate benchmark_scores; these are the reference baselines.
context_length: Not an embedding/LLM model; the scorer runs on tokenized chunks. 600s execution time limit on Codalab py37 docker. Gold chunk token length |g| is the only length that matters for the 0.40 threshold.
gain_evidence: The metric is fully understood and exploitable. Because a whole-doc submitted chunk fully satisfies overlap >= 0.40 for every gold chunk inside it (LCSseq non-contiguous), the CHUNKS_F2MACRO can be effectively solved by a good DOC-level retriever. Concretely: emit one whole-doc chunk per submitted doc; then CHUNKS_F2 roughly equals the doc-level "chunk-coverage" of submitted relevant docs. The known danger: extra non-gold docs drag BOTH doc precision and (via their chunks) chunk precision down. If you raise doc F2 by X, chunk F2 rises similarly because the chunk signal is derivative of doc selection. Expected gain vs baseline 0.3764: pushing DOCS_F2 from 0.5587 toward ceiling (~0.9+) and CHUNKS_F2 from 0.1941 to approx equal DOCS_F2 (because whole-doc chunks recover per-doc chunks) could take FINAL_SCORE to ~0.85+. This is the single highest-leverage insight: the chunk metric is almost free once doc retrieval is good, given you emit whole-doc chunks.
compute_cost: Negligible model compute; the scorer run-time is bounded by the 600s Codalab limit. Local CPU suffices to reproduce the scorer (pip install rapidfuzz==2.15.2 tokenizers==0.13.3) and empirically calibrate overhead. No GPU needed.
dev_proxy_strategy: Build a local replica of the scorer: install rapidfuzz==2.15.2 and tokenizers==0.13.3, implement overlap=LCSseq.similarity(c,g)/len(g_tokens)>=0.40, compute macro F2 per query. Use BM25 auto-pseudo-labels (chunks predicted gold) on a held-out set to derive an authoritative calculator offline. Brute-force the edge cases (|G|=0, empty D, duplicate chunks, many-chunk-matching-one-gold) against a fake gold set to confirm handling before committing a strategy.
risk: Metric misread (the stated top risk). (1) Most common: thinking LCS must be CONTIGUOUS (it is not) -> underestimates chunk recall, causing over-chunking. (2) Misreading that chunks are compared across the whole doc corpus or cross-doc (they are same-query + same-doc_id only) -> could dedup/merge wrongly. (3) Misreading that overlap uses normalized_similarity (divides by max) instead of similarity/|g| (divides by gold length) -> changes every threshold. (4) Misreading the token unit: subword vs word tokens changes |g| and materially laxes/tightens the 0.40 threshold (scorer_tokenizer_identity uncertain). (5) Submitting chunks for non-gold docs: guaranteed precision loss. (6) Submitting duplicates/many-overlapping-chunks per doc: guaranteed precision loss with no recall gain. (7) "query with no gold" handling unknown -> adds risk to over-submitting to rare/no-gold queries.
integration_notes: Scoring is the OFFICIAL BTC; we do not modify it. Integration: (1) pip install rapidfuzz==2.15.2 tokenizers==0.13.3 in a local venv; (2) write scripts/score_local.py replicating: for each query, load D (submitted doc_ids + chunks), load G (gold doc_ids + gold chunks from a local sample), compute doc P/R/F2 and chunk P/R/F2, average -> FINAL_SCORE; (3) use this local scorer on held-out pseudo-gold to tune chunking; candidates = (a) one-whole-doc-chunk-per-doc, (b) fixed-window slides (e.g. 512 tokens / 25% overlap), (c) mixed; (4) adopt whichever maximizes the local replica; (5) the submission writer should emit ONE whole-doc chunk per chosen doc (or a tuned window), never duplicates.
decision: adopt - fully map the metric and use the "whole-doc chunk per predicted-gold doc" strategy because the non-contiguous LCSseq + same-doc matching makes chunk recall essentially free once doc retrieval is correct; build a local replica scorer to de-risk edge cases.
sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rapidfuzz/RapidFuzz/main/CHANGELOG.rst (confirms rapidfuzz.distance.LCSseq.similarity = length of longest common subsequence, order-preserving, not contiguous; module present since v2.0.0 and stable through 2.15.x; normalized_similarity divides by max(len1,len2))
Live verification: python rapidfuzz 3.14.6 LCSseq.similarity("abxcd","abycdf") = 4; normalized_similarity = 0.6667 (max-denominator)
